memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are to slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and then Aaron's sons the priests shall bring the blood and splash it against the sides of the altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting.'" - Lev 1:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who does the killing. Not the priest — the worshipper. The man who brought the bull was the man who took its life. God would not let him stand at a comfortable distance while somebody else handled the unpleasant part.

This was deliberate. Worship in Israel was not tidy. It involved noise, blood, and the smell of death. Every visit to the tabernacle reminded the worshipper that his sin had a body count.

Then the priests took over. The worshipper could kill, but he could not approach the altar. Only the appointed mediators could handle the blood and bring it near to God. Even in the act of atonement, the sinner needed someone to go between.

Both roles meet in Jesus. Our sin sent Him to the cross — Isaiah says He was pierced for our transgressions (Isa 53:5), and we cannot hold ourselves at a distance from that. Yet He is also our great High Priest, the one Mediator between God and mankind (1 Tim 2:5; Heb 4:14), carrying His own blood into God's presence on our behalf.

The bloodiness of Leviticus is not primitive. It is honest. And it makes the cross make sense.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I ever treat my sin as though it were somebody else's problem?
2. What difference does it make that Jesus is both my sacrifice and my priest?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me never to look at the cross casually. Thank You that Jesus carried what I could never carry to You. Amen.
